nettyIngressContract.scope: Executable actual-Netty buffer ingress ownership contract. The copied small ingress boundary has no Minecraft/native peer context; peer join/tracking/pickup/teardown and certified chat remain UNRUN.

earlierAttempt.outcome: Seven primary checks passed, then the test expectation caught RuntimeException only; actual Netty throws a sneaky checked ClosedChannelException. R2 catches Exception. No fixture/production change. Modern r1 unrun.

limits: Primary passes with ingot 1, ordinary furnace return 1, raw iron 0, health 20, empty cursor and stopped navigation. Debit and bedrock placement share END 150; removal is END 403, return END 412 and final valid history END 418.

Primary completion excludes requests through sequence 19, pins post-idle server tick 417 at sequence 20 and accepts sequence 22 with END 418. This witnesses the corrected completion fence in actual gameplay.

Modern fails after the placement hand loses its original ownership rights. Its last copied server observation precedes placement, with ingot 0 and raw iron/furnace 1. Packet-fed block observations then report a furnace before the pause. No owned cleanup receipt is present.

The precise modern rights-loss predicate is not logged. Input replacement, selected slot, manual keys, menu, stack/layout and context guards must be distinguished before a behavior change. The generic pause alone does not identify the cause.
The earlier 14c primary assertion failure remains retained; it is distinct from the new modern product guard refusal. Neither is converted into a pass.
Both exact builds and 313/268 checks pass. The 24-job CI matrix is still running in this snapshot; completed jobs do not establish the remaining profiles.

Two original gameplay captures pass anonymous size/hash read-back and signed-out 640x360 decoding. Four exact local original/staging PNG copies are removed. Worlds, logs, icons, receipts and frozen artifacts remain.

The Netty probe executes eight buffer ownership cases on each exact dependency version: normal consumption, encoding failure, closed before allocation, closed after encoding, consuming exception, reentrant refusal, decoder exception and framework closed-channel rejection. It does not execute the native peer helper.

The first probe caught only RuntimeException and missed Netty’s sneaky checked ClosedChannelException after seven primary passes. Its source and failure log remain; R2 corrects the probe expectation and passes all sixteen cases without any product change.
No supplied fixture proves natural gameplay, a certified remote peer or user acceptance. Cooperative actor integration and the remaining parity groups are open.
